messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High error rate on serving-runtime pool gpu-pool-7 — multiple container restarts detected (OOM during prefill). Severity: P1. Paging oncall.
sre-mia: Acked. I'm oncall and jumping in. Anyone seeing customer reports? :phone:
support-kevin: A few customers reported streaming disconnects and 'internal server error' 502s from /v1/generate in the last 3m. One prod tenant (acme-markets) saw retries. Sending details to support thread.
runtime-raj: grabbing logs from the affected node now. preliminary: repeated CUDA OOM during prefill for long-context jobs (~> 120k tokens window attempts) then container restart loop.
runtime-raj: log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T02:12:45Z model-server[pid=2345]: prefill: allocate KV cache len=131072
2026-03-17T02:12:45Z model-server[pid=2345]: cuda runtime error: out of memory (function=alloc_kv_cache)
2026-03-17T02:12:45Z systemd: container exited with code 137
2026-03-17T02:12:46Z orchestrator: restarting container (attempt 3)
```
sre-mia: thanks. That lines up with the alert. What's the traffic pattern — surge or single heavy job? any noisy tenant?
ml-amy: checking model telemetry — appears these were mostly requests for the large-context endpoint with user-supplied long documents and embeddings combined (prefill + embed call pattern). One tenant is doing a batched import that spiked token counts.
support-kevin: acme-markets is likely the tenant. They started a migration import job 02:10 UTC.
runtime-raj: immediate mitigation suggestions:
- throttle/limit prefill token length at the gateway for the affected route (max_input_tokens=65536) and reject/return 413 for larger.
- enable streaming-trim for long requests (drop prefix when streaming buffer full)
- temporarily route heavy long-context traffic to CPU fallback nodes (slower but avoids GPU crash)
- config: set env PREFILL_KV_ALLOC_RETRY=3 and PREFILL_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.7
sre-mia: let's triage in order. Can infra-bot patch the route to enforce max_input_tokens? That is fastest.
infra-bot: /ops patch-route --route /v1/large-context --set max_input_tokens=65536 --user=oncall
infra-bot: route patched, rollout started (canary on 3 pods). monitoring for 30s.
runtime-raj: also toggled ephemeral KVCACHE eviction policy on the pool to 'aggressive' for node gpu-pool-7 to free prefix space. Command run:
```
kubectl exec -n inference svc/runtime-config -- ./set-kv-eviction --pool gpu-pool-7 --policy aggressive
```
ml-amy: enabling CPU fallback for oversized prefill requests now (policy: prefer-cpu-for-prefill=true). This will still serve but at much higher latency.
sre-mia: good. Support, please notify acme-markets that we're throttling large imports and providing a slower fallback; we want them to pause the import if possible.
support-kevin: contacting them now. I'll escalate and ask them to pause the import. ETA 3-5m for response.
eng-lead-sam: long-term we should add a protective admission filter at the API edge to break up massive prefill requests into safe chunks or reject with clear error and suggested retry strategy. Filing a ticket after incident.
sre-mia: monitoring metrics: container restarts dropped to 0 in last 60s on patched nodes. Error rate for /v1/generate down 78%.
support-kevin: acme confirmed they paused the job. They saw 5 failed requests, will retry with smaller batches. They appreciate the fast response.
runtime-raj: followups before we close:
- revert aggressive eviction after 1h if stable
- add a per-tenant long-request quota and alert when exceeded
- add clearer 413 payload to SDK docs
ml-amy: we'll also run a quick sim in staging to reproduce the prefill OOM with the same model + token sizes and check whether quantization or KV compression helps.
sre-mia: handing off to eng-lead-sam for overnight watch and post-incident writeup. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
eng-lead-sam: taking handoff. I'll kick off the incident timeline and postmortem doc. If anything flares, ping me directly. Off to triage the root cause with runtime & ml.
incident-bot: Incident marked as 'mitigated' at 3740003368 (actions: route throttle, CPU fallback, KV eviction). Please file follow-up playbook items: edge admission, per-tenant quotas, staging repro.
